messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batching path (us-west-2) p99 latency spike above SLO. p95 ~ 850ms, p99 ~ 6.3s, streaming stalls observed. Auto page triggered.
ashley (oncall): ack. looking. setting priority=high. paging raj.
raj: I'm on. grabbing stack and recent deploys. any error rates? customer errors?
ashley (oncall): client errors low (4xx unchanged). saw increase in request queuing on batcher and backend kv evictions spikes in logs.
cheng: logs show repeated pack-assembly timeouts ~300ms on cont-batch worker -> queue piles. KV cache eviction heat around 02:14 UTC.
sasha: looks like mixed sequence-length load ramped (many long-context requests) plus a batch_size cap interaction. pack_shed didn't kick in early.
emily: pushing current metrics dashboard: https://graf.redwood/contbatch/usw2/latency - can everyone look at requests/sec and batch-size distribution?
(ops-bot reacts :eyes:)
raj: verified – median batch size jumped from 6 -> 18 in 90s window; scheduler backlog increased, streaming consumers blocked waiting for batch fill. That explains p99 tail.
ashley (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily lower cont_batch.max_size to 8; 2) enable pack_shed aggressive mode on worker pool; 3) increment scheduler fairness weight for streaming to favor low-latency shards; 4) spin up 2 extra dedicated GPUs in fallback pool. will run steps in that order.
cheng: running command to update config on pool-prod-usw2: ```sh
redwoodctl cfg set cont_batch.max_size=8 --env=prod --region=us-west-2
```
cheng: applied. confirmation: cont_batch.max_size=8 on 8/10 nodes. rolling to remaining nodes.
raj: enabling pack_shed aggressive -> ```sh
redwoodctl ops pack-shed enable --pool contbatch-usw2 --mode aggressive
```
raj: pack_shed enabled on all workers. logging shows immediate drop in assembly latency.
sasha: adjusted scheduler weights: streaming_priority += 0.25 on scheduler groups handling websocket streams.
emily: spun up 2 nodes in fallback-dedicated-gpu pool; autoscaling shows nodes healthy. route table updated to accept burst traffic.
ashley (oncall): monitoring... p99 falling: 6.3s -> 1.8s in 40s, p95 now ~560ms. still above SLO target of 500ms but improving.
olivia (product-cc): any customers impacted? which tenants saw degraded latency? need list for comms.
raj: tenant list: 7 tenants had >2s p99: alpha-inc, betalabs, marketface, quickchat, secure-docs, nova-ai, demo-org. only alpha-inc and betalabs reported slow responses.
ashley (oncall): notify SOC + account execs for alpha-inc and betalabs; olivia will draft message.
olivia (product-cc): drafting. will say partial degraded latency, mitigation in progress, next update in 30m.
ops-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/contbatch-tail-latency. recommended postmortem owner: @cheng.
ashley (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall: we lowered max_size to 8 and enabled aggressive pack_shed; scheduler weights bumped for streaming; fallback pool up. watch for reversion effects and kv cache churn. if p99 > 2s for >10m, escalate to infra oncall (ping infra-sig).
raj: leaving handoff to cheng for deeper root cause. I'll monitor for 10m then stand down.
cheng: taking ownership for post-incident RCA. initial hypothesis: sequence-length distribution burst plus batching policy edge-case prevented timely pack_shed and led to assembly queuing -> streaming stalls. next steps: repro in staging with long-tail traffic generator; add safety guard to pack_assembly latency to preemptive shed when assembly > 200ms; consider adaptive max_size based on seq-len histogram.
sasha: also propose scheduler fairness bug fix: weights not applied to cross-shard streaming groups under heavy load. I'll open a PR after triage.
nashley (oncall): closing page for now, incident state = mitigated. we'll keep thread open for RCA updates. :white_check_mark:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded.
_meta: generated for dataset: contbatch tail latency incident thread
